cues.en: And the key to answering these questions were in these two concepts that you may have heard before, rediscovering

cues.en: What I wanted to accomplish with this new Zelda was to create a game where the user can truly experience freedom in an expansive play field.
cues.zh: 在这部新的《Zelda》中，我想实现的是打造一款让玩家能在广阔世界中真正体验到自由的游戏。

cues.en: And through exploring this field, I wanted the user to be able to experience a new sense of adventure again and again and be able to freely navigate through it as they see fit.
cues.zh: 通过探索这片广袤原野，我希望玩家能一次又一次获得全新的冒险体验，并能完全随心所欲地自由穿行。

cues.en: A game where the user can think and decide on their own where they want to go and what they want to do and experience excitement and adventure.
cues.zh: 一款玩家可以自行思考和决定想去哪里、想做什么，并体验刺激与冒险的游戏。

cues.en: But I realized that to create a game in which, as I mentioned earlier, the user can think and decide on their own where they want to go and what they want to do,
cues.zh: 但我意识到，要做出这样一款游戏——正如我之前提到的，让玩家自己思考、自己决定想去哪里、想做什么——

cues.zh: 还有不少难关需要克服。

cues.en: Not
cues.zh: 不能

cues.en: being able to move forward with an event without having followed a set path.
cues.zh: 不按既定路线走就无法推进事件。

cues.en: Having walls that you can't get around due to level design.
cues.zh: 由于关卡设计的原因，存在无法绕过的墙壁。

cues.en: Or it could be that unless you've gone through a predetermined set of experiences,
cues.zh: 或者可能是，除非玩家经历了一系列预设的体验，

cues.zh: 这些都是《塞尔达传说》以往的惯例。

cues.en: So our first step in designing the game was to reexamine these conventions
cues.zh: 所以我们在设计游戏时的第一步，就是重新审视这些惯例，

cues.en: and put our sights on changing the structure of the game from a passive one where you play within the confines of a pre prepared mechanism,
cues.zh: 并将目标转向改变游戏的结构，不再让你局限在预设的机制中被动游玩，

cues.en: to one where the user can actively engage with the game.
cues.zh: 而是打造一个玩家能主动参与其中的游戏。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: what is an active game?
cues.zh: 什么是“主动型游戏”呢？

cues.en: Our first approach was to remove those impassable walls, which were a convention of Zelda,
cues.zh: 我们最初的做法，是打破《塞尔达传说》惯有的那些“不可逾越之墙”，

cues.en: by transforming the walls and allowing the user to climb them in our experimental game field.
cues.zh: 通过改造这些墙体，让玩家能在我们的实验性游戏场景中攀爬它们。

cues.en: By transforming walls, were used to represent boundaries,
cues.zh: 通过改造墙壁——那些原本用来表示边界的墙——

cues.en: into another optional path, it's as if the entire landscape delays before the user opens up asking them, so which path are you going to take?
cues.zh: 把它变成另一条可选路径，就好像整个场景在用户打开之前先做了延迟，然后问他们：你要走哪条路？

cues.en: And it was at this point that I realized
cues.zh: 而正是在这一刻我意识到

cues.en: this was the kind of game design I was striving for and holds the potential to create this active game I had envisioned.
cues.zh: 这正是我一直追求的那种游戏设计，它有可能创造出我曾设想的那种主动式游戏。

cues.en: First step, And
cues.zh: 第一步，而且

cues.zh: 所以很自然地，当你爬上一座高山的山顶向下看时，

cues.zh: 你真正能做的事只有一件。于是你

cues.zh: 通过加入一个动作，让你能借助道具在空中滑翔，

cues.en: once you climb, you can fly to wherever you want.
cues.zh: 爬上去之后，你就能飞到想去的任何地方。

cues.en: I felt that this was the crucial ingredient that will expand the sense of freedom in the new Zelda.
cues.zh: 我觉得，这是拓展新《塞尔达》自由感的关键要素。

cues.en: After witnessing a simple multiplication
cues.zh: 在见识到玩家的行动

cues.en: Many puzzles found in Zelda games are based on things like natural phenomena or simple science facts that don't require a lot of prior knowledge.
cues.zh: 《塞尔达》游戏中的很多谜题，都是基于自然现象或简单的科学常识，不需要太多先验知识。

cues.en: But with the way we had been building games thus far, we were using each of these individually as clues or hints to to solve puzzles.
cues.zh: 但在我们以往做游戏的方式中，都是把它们单独作为解谜的线索或提示来用的。

cues.en: It's not a stretch to say that the objects that made up each of these puzzles were made specifically for those puzzles.
cues.zh: 毫不夸张地说，构成这些谜题的物件，完全就是为这些谜题量身定做的。

cues.en: This, of course, allows us to fine tune and polish the gameplay experience,
cues.zh: 这当然能让我们精心调优并打磨游戏体验，

cues.en: but unfortunately,
cues.zh: 但遗憾的是，

cues.en: it requires a lot of resource, and this mess... Method of development by addition was not going to work for the new Zelda.
cues.zh: 这需要耗费大量资源，而这种“加法式”的开发方……方法，在新的《塞尔达》里是行不通的。

cues.en: So my next thought was, I wonder if I can use this idea of multiplication
cues.zh: 于是我又想，能不能用这种乘法的思路

cues.en: and and apply it to the mass production of these puzzles.
cues.zh: 把它应用到这些谜题的量产上。

cues.en: Make the game so that objects react to the player's action and the objects themselves also influence each other.
cues.zh: 让游戏里的物体对玩家的动作做出反应，而且物体之间也相互影响。

cues.en: If we could do this, I felt that we might be one step closer to creating an active game.
cues.zh: 如果能做到这一点，我觉得我们或许就离打造一款动态游戏更近一步了。

cues.en: So I had to find out if applying this hypothesis to Zelda and implementing this multiplicative gameplay will actually result in an active game.
cues.zh: 所以我必须弄清楚，把这个假设应用到 Zelda 上、实现这种乘法式玩法，是否真的能带来一款动态游戏。

cues.en: I decided to experiment with this in the simplest way possible.
cues.zh: 我决定用最简单的方式来尝试这件事。

cues.en: The ways we solve these challenges make for interesting stories in and of themselves,
cues.zh: 我们解决这些挑战的过程本身就很有意思，

cues.en: but we're a bit pressed for time here. Someday if we have the chance, I'd love to tell you all about it.
cues.zh: 但今天时间有点紧，以后有机会的话，我很想好好跟各位聊聊。

cues.en: So I'd like to talk today about how we went about realizing this idea of multiplicative gameplay that Mr. Fujibashi mentioned previously.
cues.zh: 今天我想聊聊，我们是如何实现藤林先生之前提到的“乘法玩法”这个理念的。

cues.en: It's actually a matter of physics and chemistry.
cues.zh: 这其实涉及物理和化学的原理。

cues.en: But don't worry, this won't be an academic lecture or anything.
cues.zh: 但别担心，这不会是学术讲座之类的。

cues.en: I consider the Legend of Zelda games to be action games.
cues.zh: 我认为《塞尔达传说》系列属于动作游戏。

cues.en: To go about our business of breaking conventions,
cues.zh: 为了打破常规，

cues.en: we decided to take a step back and think about the most primitive elements of action games.
cues.zh: 我们决定退一步，思考动作游戏最原始的元素。

cues.en: In
cues.zh: 从

cues.en: its most basic components, an action game is made up of collision,
cues.zh: 最基础的组件来看，动作游戏是由碰撞、

cues.en: movement, and object states.
cues.zh: 移动和物体状态构成的。

cues.en: Taken together, collision and movement make up what we call physics in games.
cues.zh: 碰撞与移动结合在一起，便构成了我们在游戏中所谓的物理。

cues.en: But of course when it comes to game development,
cues.zh: 但显而易见的是，在游戏开发领域，

cues.en: you don't want the sort of physics you find in a textbook,
cues.zh: 你并不需要教科书里那种物理，

cues.en: but a kind that fits the needs of the game you're making.
cues.zh: 而是需要符合当前游戏需求的物理。

cues.en: And this is what we call game physics. Since the NES era, a plethora of games have added to our understanding of this concept of game physics.
cues.zh: 这也就是我们所说的游戏物理。自红白机（NES）时代以来，无数的游戏不断加深着我们对“游戏物理”这一概念的理解。

cues.en: Game physics could also be called false physics or liar's physics.
cues.zh: 游戏物理也可以被称为虚假物理，或“骗子的物理”。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: why would you need to tell lies?
cues.zh: 为什么需要“说谎”呢？

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is something we do to increase controllability and responsiveness.
cues.zh: 其实是为了提升操控感和响应性。

cues.en: In other words, to fulfill the demands of game design.
cues.zh: 换句话说，就是为了满足游戏设计的需求。

cues.en: We
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: also end up telling these lies to optimize processing power and sometimes even to increase the sense of realism.
cues.zh: 有时也是为了优化处理性能，甚至是为了增加真实感而“说谎”。

cues.en: On the other hand, if we're telling lies, what use do we have for the laws of physics?
cues.zh: 但反过来说，如果我们都在“说谎”，那物理定律对我们又有什么用呢？

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: think it's so that we can build a sense of trust between the player and the game. Players encounter in game events they've observed in the real world and come to believe in the game's particular set of rules.
cues.zh: 我觉得这是为了在玩家和游戏之间建立一种信任感。玩家在游戏中遇到现实世界里见过的现象，就会开始相信这款游戏特有的一套规则。

cues.en: And that's the basis for the clever lies we tell in games.
cues.zh: 这就是我们在游戏里编织巧妙谎言的基础。

cues.en: And of course, the Zelda series is no exception to this. Past titles have made ample use of game physics to make performing actions and solving puzzles more intuitive.
cues.zh: 当然，塞尔达系列也不例外。以往的作品大量运用游戏物理，让玩家更直观地完成操作、解开谜题。

cues.en: One of the joys of being a programmer is deciding just how to go about telling our clever lies and how to best express the things that happen in an imaginary world.
cues.zh: 作为程序员，一大乐趣就是决定如何巧妙地编织谎言，又如何最好地呈现那些发生在虚构世界里的事情。

cues.en: Given that this game was supposed to take place in a vast world,
cues.zh: 既然这款游戏的舞台设定在一个广阔的世界里，

cues.en: I felt it deserved a correspondingly robust game physics that would help bring it to life.
cues.zh: 我觉得它也应该有一套足够完善的游戏物理系统，让这个世界鲜活起来。

cues.en: On the other hand, creating a high degree of freedom had been an important theme for us since the earliest stages of development.
cues.zh: 另一方面，从开发初期开始，为玩家提供高度自由就是我们的重要目标。

cues.en: For example, the freedom to carry any object you like to any location in the game.
cues.zh: 比如，你可以自由地把任何物品带到游戏里的任何地方。

cues.en: If you try hard enough, you can roll this rock from the beginning of the game
cues.zh: 只要你足够努力，甚至能把这块石头从游戏开局

cues.en: to the place you fight the final boss.
cues.zh: 一路滚到最终 Boss 战的地方。

cues.en: But of course, in a physics simulation,
cues.zh: 但显然，在物理模拟中，

cues.en: you have to make this sort of thing possible in a set of complex and near infinite situations.
cues.zh: 你必须在各种复杂且近乎无限的情境下，让这种事情成为可能。

cues.en: The development resources associated with creating this type of physics simulation would be immense,
cues.zh: 开发这种物理模拟所需的资源量是极其庞大的，

cues.en: but we were dead set on making the physics in this game fun.
cues.zh: 但我们铁了心要把这款游戏的物理系统做得好玩。

cues.en: We realized that if we continued using the same approach we had in previous games, we'd run out of steam long before reaching our goal.
cues.zh: 我们意识到，如果继续沿用之前游戏中的同一种方法，我们早就坚持不到达成目标了。

cues.en: And so, after running some tests, we decided to use Havoc to help create our physics simulation.
cues.zh: 因此，在进行了一些测试之后，我们决定使用 Havoc 来帮助创建物理模拟。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 该

cues.en: stability and robustness of the engine, not to mention its proven track record in the game industry, made Havoc an appealing choice. This would enable us to tell all the clever lies we wanted.
cues.zh: 引擎的稳定性和鲁棒性，更不用说它在游戏行业中经过验证的良好记录，使得 Havoc 成为一个有吸引力的选择。这将使我们能够讲述我们想要的所有巧妙的谎言。

cues.en: Most of the actions and items we've introduced in Breath of the Wild rely heavily on game physics.
cues.zh: 《旷野之息》中我们介绍的大多数动作和道具，都高度依赖游戏物理。

cues.en: This came from being able to focus our efforts on the elements we most wanted to make.
cues.zh: 这是因为我们能集中精力，打造自己最想实现的元素。

cues.en: Let
cues.zh: 我来

cues.en: me show you a few examples.
cues.zh: 给你们看几个例子。

cues.en: First
cues.zh: 首先

cues.en: is stasis,
cues.zh: 是静止器，

cues.en: a rune that allows you to stop the effects of time on specific objects.
cues.zh: 它是一种符文，可以让特定物体停止受时间影响。

cues.en: It may look as though it simply stopped,
cues.zh: 它看起来好像只是停住了，

cues.en: but internally the object is working hard to maintain its stasis.
cues.zh: 但实际上，物体内部正努力维持着静止状态。

cues.en: It's
cues.zh: 这就是

cues.en: the law of comfort... Conservation of energy,
cues.zh: 舒适守恒定律……能量守恒定律，

cues.en: except really that's a lie.
cues.zh: 不过其实这完全是骗人的。

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 它

cues.en: feels right in the moment it happens but makes less sense the more you stop and think about it.
cues.zh: 发生的那一刻感觉挺对，但你越琢磨就越觉得说不通。

cues.en: Game physics are at their best when they let you create things like this that can't exist in reality.
cues.zh: 游戏物理最妙的地方，就在于能让你做出这种现实中根本不可能存在的东西。

cues.en: Next up is Magnesis,
cues.zh: 接下来是磁力抓取器（Magnesis），

cues.en: a rune which allows you to move metal objects at will.
cues.zh: 这个符文能让你随心所欲地移动金属物体。

cues.en: It looks like magnetism,
cues.zh: 它看起来像磁力，

cues.en: but it isn't actually.
cues.zh: 但其实并不是。

cues.en: Instead, it's something like magnetism.
cues.zh: 准确地说，它只是某种类似磁力的东西。

cues.en: The point here is to prevent instability from a programming perspective without sacrificing control for the player.
cues.zh: 这里的重点是从编程角度防止不稳定，同时不牺牲玩家的操控权。

cues.en: And here's the rock climbing that mister Fujibashi also mentioned.
cues.zh: 这就是藤林先生也提到的攀岩。

cues.en: By creating a dynamic constraint between Link and the surface he's climbing, we connect him to it. The programmer in charge of this climbing movement really focused on getting it right and thanks to that effort, we were able to make Link climb moving objects in a satisfying way. And it's Havoc that did the work of solving the issue of constraint for us.
cues.zh: 通过在 Link 和他攀爬的表面之间建立动态约束，我们把他和表面连接起来。负责这个攀爬移动的程序员非常专注于把它做对，多亏了这份努力，我们才能让 Link 以令人满意的方式攀爬移动的物体。而正是 Havoc 为我们解决了约束问题。

cues.en: The act of cutting down a tree is made possible by a false sort of destruction.
cues.zh: 砍倒一棵树，靠的是一种虚假的毁灭。

cues.en: The moment the tree begins to fall,
cues.zh: 树开始倒下的那一刻，

cues.en: it transforms into a log object.
cues.zh: 它就变成了一根原木。

cues.en: When the log falls into the water, it floats.
cues.zh: 原木掉进水里后，会漂浮起来。

cues.en: This ability to float in water holds an important meaning for game design.
cues.zh: 这种在水中漂浮的能力，对游戏设计意义重大。

cues.en: When an object floats in the game, it means you've invented a unique but illusory kind of floating.
cues.zh: 物体在游戏中漂浮，意味着你创造了一种独特却虚幻的漂浮方式。

cues.en: Now I'd like to get back to the theme of multiplicative gameplay that mister Fujibashi
cues.zh: 现在，我想回到藤桥先生提到的

cues.en: mentioned.
cues.zh: 乘法式玩法这个主题。

cues.en: In our various experiments of trial and error with game physics, there was one thing that we noticed.
cues.zh: 在针对游戏物理系统反复试错的过程中，我们注意到了这么一件事。

cues.en: If you unify your game world with a set of consistent physics rules, the player will come up with ideas for all sorts of things they want to try.
cues.zh: 如果你用一套一致的物理规则来统一整个游戏世界，玩家就会冒出各种想要尝试的新想法。

cues.en: So for example, this metal slab is placed here to allow you to cross this river.
cues.zh: 举个例子，这块金属板原本是放在这儿让你过河用的。

cues.en: But once you pick it up, you might find yourself suddenly wanting to try dropping it on top of an enemy.
cues.zh: 但一旦你把它拿起来，可能就会突然想试试把它砸在敌人头上。

cues.en: Once you see that log floating on the river, it's natural to want to try jumping on it.
cues.zh: 一旦你看到那根木头漂在河上，自然会想试着跳上去。

cues.en: Just riding a log down a river seems like it would be fun. You might remember this from the prototype earlier.
cues.zh: 顺流踩着木头漂下去，似乎挺好玩。你可能还记得之前原型里的这个。

cues.en: And if you can climb moving objects,
cues.zh: 而如果你能攀爬移动的物体，

cues.en: what sort of battle would unfold if you were fighting a giant enemy that you could climb?
cues.zh: 那么当你与一个可以攀爬的巨大敌人战斗时，会展开怎样的战斗呢？

cues.en: What would happen if you climbed an object that you'd charged up with energy using stasis?
cues.zh: 如果你爬上一个你用静止术充能过的物体，会发生什么？

cues.en: My point is that I ended up getting flooded with ideas like this.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，后来我脑子里涌现出一大堆这样的想法。

cues.en: My excitement was coming not from my perspective as a developer, but as a player.
cues.zh: 让我兴奋的不是开发者的视角，而是玩家的视角。

cues.en: What if I tried that? Or wait, maybe this.
cues.zh: 要不试试这个？等等，或许试试这个。

cues.en: This would be a world where combining simple elements could produce complex results,
cues.zh: 这是一个只要组合简单元素，就能产生复杂结果的世界，

cues.en: where you'd feel the thrill of imagining the things you wanted to try as you played.
cues.zh: 在这里，游玩时你会因为想象着想尝试的各种玩法而感到兴奋。

cues.en: I realized that was the game we should try to make.
cues.zh: 我意识到，这就是我们应该尝试制作的游戏。

cues.en: Okay. Now I'd like to switch topics a bit. These two are members of our development team.
cues.zh: 好了，现在我想稍微换个话题。这两位是我们开发团队的成员。

cues.en: They're discussing just how we should go about breaking these conventions of ours.
cues.zh: 他们正在讨论我们究竟该如何打破现有的这些常规。

cues.en: Looks like they're having a good time.
cues.zh: 看起来他们聊得很开心。

cues.en: This must be a heartfelt conversation.
cues.zh: 这一定是一次推心置腹的交流。

cues.en: Okay. Now it looks like things are really heating up. It was during this discussion that a certain keyword was born.
cues.zh: 好了，现在气氛看起来真的热烈起来了。正是在这次讨论中，诞生了一个关键词。

cues.en: If physics engines are such a thing, why don't you ever hear about chemistry engines?
cues.zh: 既然物理引擎这么普遍，那为什么从来没听说过化学引擎呢？

cues.en: As you likely know, the Zelda series has long made use of the sort of events that occur in chemistry as in game elements.
cues.zh: 你可能知道，塞尔达系列长期以来一直把化学中发生的那种事件当作游戏元素来用。

cues.en: Just
cues.zh: 就

cues.en: like with physics, creating puzzles with solutions that reference the way the real world works can help players solve them instinctively.
cues.zh: 像物理一样，设计谜题时让解法参照现实世界的运作方式，能帮玩家凭直觉解开。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: so we decided to develop a chemistry engine.
cues.zh: 所以我们决定开发一个化学引擎。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: what exactly is this chemistry engine?
cues.zh: 这个化学引擎到底是什么？

cues.en: One
cues.zh: 一

cues.en: way of describing physics engine is as a rule based movement calculator.
cues.zh: 种描述物理引擎的方式，是把它看作基于规则的运动计算器。

cues.en: In comparison,
cues.zh: 相比之下，

cues.en: we decided the chemistry engine would be a rule based state calculator.
cues.zh: 我们决定把化学引擎设计成基于规则的状态计算器。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: mentioned this before, but action games are made up of collision plus movement plus changing states.
cues.zh: 之前提过，动作游戏由碰撞、移动和状态变化组成。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: it's our chemistry engine that calculates these changes in the state of things.
cues.zh: 这些事物的状态变化，都是由我们的化学引擎计算的。

cues.en: So I'd like to give a simple explanation of our design to show just what sort of calculations are being run by this chemistry engine.
cues.zh: 所以我想简单介绍一下我们的设计，说明化学引擎究竟在进行哪些计算。

cues.en: First, we refer to things like fire, water, and ice that don't hold a constant solid form as elements.
cues.zh: 首先，我们将火、水、冰这类没有固定固体形态的东西称为“元素”。

cues.en: Next we call solid objects like trees and rocks,
cues.zh: 接着，我们把树木、岩石这类固体物件，

cues.en: even the player
cues.zh: 甚至是玩家

cues.en: character and weapons materials.
cues.zh: 角色和武器，统称为“材质”。

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 这套

cues.en: chemistry engine uses these things to make its calculations based on three simple rules.
cues.zh: 化学引擎就是基于三条简单规则，利用这些对象来进行计算的。

cues.en: First up is rule one. Elements can change the state of materials.
cues.zh: 首先是第一条规则：元素可以改变材质的状态。

cues.en: So the leaves on the tree burn up and disappear.
cues.zh: 比如树上的叶子会被烧掉并消失。

cues.en: Next is rule two. Elements are able to change each other's states.
cues.zh: 接下来是第二条规则。元素能够改变彼此的状态。

cues.en: So the fire disappeared when it came in contact with the water.
cues.zh: 所以火接触到水时就消失了。

cues.en: And finally, rule three.
cues.zh: 最后是第三条规则。

cues.en: Materials cannot influence each other's states.
cues.zh: 物质不能影响彼此的状态。

cues.en: So you can see neither of them changed.
cues.zh: 所以你可以看到两者都没有变化。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: that's the chemistry engine in a nutshell.
cues.zh: 这就是化学引擎的简要概括。

cues.en: The model is an extremely simple one but allows for the expression of all sorts of events.
cues.zh: 这个模型极其简单，却能表达各种各样的事件。

cues.en: All these types of interactions in the game are realized by the chemistry engine.
cues.zh: 游戏里所有这些类型的交互都是由化学引擎实现的。

cues.en: Wait. Are electricity and wind a part of chemistry?
cues.zh: 等等，电和风属于化学吗？

cues.en: In a textbook, the answer is of course no, but in the chemistry engine, you bet they are.
cues.zh: 在教科书里，答案当然是否定的；但在化学引擎里，它们当然算。

cues.en: Aside from rigid body dynamics,
cues.zh: 除了刚体动力学之外，

cues.en: we consider all phenomena that occur in nature to be chemistry.
cues.zh: 我们把自然界中发生的一切现象都视为化学。

cues.en: And so for our purposes, things like wind and electricity are all considered to be elements.
cues.zh: 因此，就我们的用途而言，风和电都被视为元素。

cues.en: Again, treating them this way gives us a simplified method with which to model the world.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这样处理能让我们用更简单的方法来模拟世界。

cues.en: It's not that we wanted to create an engine that replicates chemistry.
cues.zh: 我们并不是想做一个复现化学规律的引擎。

cues.en: Instead, we wanted to create a state calculator
cues.zh: 相反，我们想做的是一个状态计算器，

cues.en: for all these objects that are connected to one another.
cues.zh: 用来处理所有这些相互关联的物体。

cues.en: There's one other reason we refer to this sort of thing as chemistry.
cues.zh: 我们把这类机制称为“化学”还有另一个原因。

cues.en: During development, we called this multiplicative gameplay we were trying to create chemical reaction play.
cues.zh: 在开发期间，我们把试图打造的这种“乘法式玩法”叫做“化学反应玩法”。

cues.en: This engine is the device that makes this sort of play possible,
cues.zh: 而这个引擎正是让这种玩法成为可能的机制，

cues.en: so in that way too, it can be considered chemistry.
cues.zh: 所以从这个角度来说，它也可以被看作是一种化学。

cues.en: Given the right situation, elements can also generate energy and impact the physical world.
cues.zh: 在合适的情境下，元素也能产生能量并影响物理世界。

cues.en: In this way all the constituent parts of the world we created are governed by our rules of physics and chemistry.
cues.zh: 这样一来，我们创造的世界中所有组成部分都受物理和化学规则支配。

cues.en: And with that, we had the game that we had hoped to make, one that used multiplication
cues.zh: 于是，我们做出了期待中的游戏，一个利用乘法

cues.en: to increase the things you were able to do.
cues.zh: 来扩展你能做的事情的游戏。

cues.en: Earlier,
cues.zh: 早些时候，

cues.en: mister Fujibashi
cues.zh: 藤林先生

cues.en: posed the question,
cues.zh: 提出了一个问题：

cues.en: how can we create a game that uses multiplication
cues.zh: 我们如何创造一款利用乘法

cues.en: to expand gameplay?
cues.zh: 来扩展玩法的游戏？

cues.en: It turns out our answer to this was to build connections between everything in the world.
cues.zh: 事实证明，我们对此的答案是：为世界上的一切建立联系。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: means that everything you see in the game is linked together, so to speak.

cues.zh: 在《风之杖 HD》开发接近尾声的某一天，《旷野之息》的总监藤林先生和制作人青沼先生把我叫了过去。

cues.zh: “对吧？”我回答。

cues.zh: 另一位美术和我完全意见一致，所以我毫不犹豫地开口了。

cues.en: Mister Aonuma said, I agree.

cues.zh: 于是

cues.zh: 整个过程不到一分钟。

cues.en: It was really surprising at the time, but looking back now and seeing how the game lost none of its originality or playability over the course of development of the Wind Waker HD,
cues.zh: 当时这让我很意外，但现在回头看，《风之杖 HD》在开发过程中并没有丢失原有的特色和可玩性，

cues.en: plus the fact that the entire staff witnessed the solidification and expansion of the game's reality day after day, our agreement on the issue seems quite natural.
cues.zh: 再加上全体工作人员每天都亲眼见证游戏世界逐渐成形、不断拓展，我们当时在这个问题上的共识也就显得很自然了。

cues.en: This is a bit off topic, but here's something that supported our common belief that we're good at this type of art creation.
cues.zh: 这有点跑题了，但有件事恰好印证了我们普遍的看法：我们确实擅长这类艺术创作。

cues.en: The difference in the evolution of painting between the West and Japan.

cues.zh: 要是深入探讨漫画和动画艺术是如何在现代日本走向更大规模、更主流的受众，那绝对会是一场非常有趣的讨论。

cues.en: But that's not why we're here, so we're gonna have to save that for another time.
cues.zh: 但这并不是我们今天的议题，所以只能留到下次再聊了。

cues.zh: 我们为什么选这句口号？

cues.zh: 其实《风之杖 HD》的美术风格有一个薄弱点。

cues.en: An important point in Mr. Fujibayashi's
cues.zh: 藤林先生游戏理念中的一个重要观点是

cues.en: game concept

cues.en: Was to fill the vast game world with fun multiplicative experiences using physics and chemistry gameplay. And
cues.zh: 用物理和化学玩法，为广阔的游戏世界填满有趣的叠加体验。而

cues.en: this was difficult to achieve with the Wind Waker HD art style.
cues.zh: 《风之杖 HD》的美术风格很难实现这一点。

cues.en: Why is that?
cues.zh: 为什么呢？

cues.en: The Wind Waker art style in its depiction of form, feel of materials, etcetera, is very stylized.
cues.zh: 《风之杖》的美术风格在形体、材质质感等方面都非常风格化。

cues.en: One
cues.zh: 其中

cues.en: of our goals was to have the was to have the art intuitively suggest possible physics and chemistry gameplay based on the player's own experiences in the real world.
cues.zh: 我们的目标之一是让美术风格能直观地提示玩家：根据他们在现实世界中的经验，可能会有哪些物理和化学玩法。

cues.en: The problem with the Wind Waker art style is the lies it told were too big.
cues.zh: 《风之杖》美术风格的问题在于，它撒的谎太大了。

cues.en: There was also another concern with the Wind Waker art style. The concern was if older players could look at the screen for just an instant and understand everything they were seeing, they might feel the art was intended for children and was not for them.
cues.zh: 对于《风之杖》的美术风格还有一个担忧：如果年长的玩家看一眼屏幕就能瞬间看懂所有东西，可能会觉得这画面是给小孩子看的，并不适合自己。

cues.en: Basing the art on something easy to tell lies with, like the wind waker art, we could more easily guarantee function conforming to playability
cues.zh: 基于容易“撒谎”的艺术形式，比如《风之杖》的风格，我们更容易保证功能契合游戏性，

cues.en: and more easily construct the reality within the game.
cues.zh: 也更容易构建游戏内的真实感。

cues.en: Above and beyond that,
cues.zh: 除此之外，

cues.en: We needed to suggest things anyone could do in the real world. So we needed a certain level of realism, and we needed an information dense, mature art style.
cues.zh: 我们还得提出任何人在现实世界里都能做到的事。所以需要一定的真实感，也需要信息密集、成熟的画风。

cues.en: Our goal of supporting these elements equally
cues.zh: 我们平等支撑这些元素的目标

cues.en: led to refreshing and full flavored.
cues.zh: 带来了清爽而饱满的风味。

cues.en: So we made this our slogan and it led to the establishment of the final art style.
cues.zh: 于是我们把它定为口号，最终确立了最终的画风。

cues.en: Shaders, lighting, models, terrain, effects, UI, weather environments,
cues.zh: 着色器、光照、模型、地形、特效、UI、天气环境，

cues.en: our slogan is the foundation upon which all these sections constructed their designs and behaviors.
cues.zh: 我们的口号是所有这些部分构建各自设计与行为的基础。

cues.en: So a fairly streamlined tempo and event presentation was necessary to efficiently present the Breath of the Wild's game tempo and game cycle.
cues.zh: 因此，我们需要采用相当简洁的节奏和事件呈现方式，高效展现《旷野之息》的游戏节奏和游戏循环。

cues.zh: 那些噗噗的烟雾和跳动的食材都被做出来时，我没觉得这荒谬，反而觉得很有意思。

cues.en: It was the moment I felt we had come up with the answer to what this game needed in its art style.
cues.zh: 那一刻我意识到，我们终于找到了这款游戏在美术风格上真正需要的东西。

cues.en: The reconciliation of the conflict between playability and reality. It's the result of our quest for art that makes it easy to lie to match this game known as Breath of the Wild.
cues.zh: 游戏性与真实感冲突之下的调和产物。这就是我们为了契合《Breath of the Wild》这款游戏，在探索如何“巧妙作假”的美术表现时所得出的答案。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is without a doubt the same trial and error process we've done throughout the history of the Zelda series.
cues.zh: 毫无疑问，这与我们在整个塞尔达系列历史中所经历的试错过程是一样的。

cues.en: The final art style appears different from any other title, but you can say it's the constant we reached as a result of our universal thought process.
cues.zh: 最终的艺术风格看起来与其他作品都不同，但可以说这是我们在通用思考过程中不断摸索后达到的必然结果。

cues.en: However, this alone does not get us to the creation of guttokuru
cues.zh: 然而，仅凭这一点还不足以创造出guttokuru

cues.en: art.
cues.zh: 艺术。

cues.zh: 你

cues.en: you understand guttokuru?
cues.zh: 理解guttokuru吗？

cues.en: In
cues.zh: 在

cues.zh: 日本，当我们回忆起触动灵魂的事物时，我们会用gutokuru这个词

cues.en: never before seen world filled with new surprises,
cues.zh: 前所未见、充满新惊喜的世界，

cues.zh: 就得打破常规。

cues.zh: 创作上得大胆放手。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.zh: 可以说，在某些方面，我们游戏创作者确实很喜欢创作暴力作品。

cues.zh: 我们的美术师是如何

cues.zh: 在作品中加入那种 guttakuru 的感觉的？在整个开发过程中，他们每天都绞尽脑汁，尽情展现自己的个性。

cues.en: I

cues.zh: 想今天在座的所有美术人员都会认同我，说这是整个过程中最令人享受的部分一点也不为过。

cues.en: While
cues.zh: 虽然

cues.zh: 艺术总监无法决定功能或指导方针，

cues.zh: 但当面临在多种美术风格或设计中做选择的机会来临时……

cues.zh: 我们确实有权释放那股近乎任性的绝对力量，去选择我们认为

cues.en: stir some souls.
cues.zh: 能震撼心灵的东西。

cues.en: I hope from the bottom of my heart that the entire world will explore the vastness of Hyrule and have their souls stirred again and again, just as I did.
cues.zh: 我衷心希望全世界的人都能探索海拉鲁的广袤，并像我一样，一次又一次被触动灵魂。

cues.en: Alright.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Let me turn it back over to the holder of the triforce
cues.zh: 让我把时间交还给拥有三角力量

cues.en: of the courage to say, mister Fujibayashi,
cues.zh: 拥有勇气之人，藤林先生，

cues.en: to wrap things up.
cues.zh: 来做总结。

cues.en: We had the triforce of courage,
cues.zh: 我们拥有勇气三角，

cues.en: the courage to be able to say whatever needs to be said to bring about a new way to play a game.
cues.zh: 有勇气说出一切必要的话，开创全新的游戏玩法。

cues.en: The Triforce of Wisdom,
cues.zh: 智慧三角，

cues.zh: 有智慧将所有游戏逻辑变为现实。

cues.zh: 还有力量三角，

cues.zh: 有力量用这一切构筑出《塞尔达》的世界。

cues.en: As you've seen in our talk today, along our path to bring this game to completion,
cues.zh: 正如大家今天在演讲中看到的，在让这款游戏走向完成的过程中，

cues.zh: 我们三人和开发团队对一些元素做出了重大改动，同时保留了其他元素原本的样子。

cues.en: I hope you were able to see that breaking conventions means to change,
cues.zh: 我希望大家能看到，打破常规意味着改变，

cues.zh: 但它也同样意味着不改变，

cues.en: to keep things as they are.
cues.zh: 保持事物的原有模样。

cues.zh: 在所有粉丝的支持下，《塞尔达传说》迎来了它的 30 周年纪念。

cues.en: Breath
cues.zh: 《旷野之息》

cues.zh: 这一漫长开发历程的集大成之作。
